# TrailingZeros 〔BlitzLLVM〕

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Math](BlitzBasic-Math)

</div>


## Command Syntax

```blitzbasic
TrailingZeros:Int32 value:Int32
```

## Description

**〔BlitzLLVM〕** This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

<!-- AUTOGENERATED COPYRIGHT HEADER START -->
Counts the bits that are 0 after the last 1, from the lowest bit up. A number of 0 has all of its bits counted. This is a BlitzLLVM extension. It looks at the bits of the number the way its type has them, so the same value counts differently as a `Byte`, an `Int` or a `Long`: a number written in the program is an `Int` (32 bits) unless it is larger, and `Byte`, `UByte`, `Short`, `UShort`, `UInt`, `Long` and `ULong` give the other widths. A real or a text is taken as an `Int`, like the bit operators do.

**Differences and known gaps:**

* Not in the originals.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | Int32 | required | An integer. |

**Returns:** How many of the lowest bits are 0.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Print TrailingZeros(8)
Print TrailingZeros(Short(0))
Print TrailingZeros(ULong(1) Shl 40)
```

```text
3
16
40
```
